narrator_001_three_packs: <speak>Three packs of hot dogs. Four in each pack.</speak>
narrator_003_cooked_myself: <speak>I know, because I cooked every one of them myself.</speak>
narrator_005_seconds: <speak>An hour later, my cousin walked to the stove for seconds, looked into the empty pot, and asked me why I'd taken two.</speak>
narrator_007_eleven_of_us: <speak>There were eleven of us in that trailer.</speak>
narrator_012_whose_face: <speak>And not one of us could tell you whose face it was wearing.</speak>
narrator_013_sixteen: <speak>I was sixteen the summer my mom sent me down from Chicago to stay with family in Alabama.</speak>
narrator_014_land: <speak>My uncle owned miles of pine woods out there, with two old camping trailers parked deep in the trees.</speak>
narrator_015_city_boy: <speak>My cousins couldn't wait to drag the city boy out into the wilderness.</speak>
narrator_016_smell: <speak>The second we got to the clearing, I noticed the smell.</speak>
narrator_017_lightning: <speak>Sharp. Metallic. Like the air right before lightning hits.</speak>
narrator_018_let_it_go: <speak>Nobody else seemed to care, so I let it go.</speak>
narrator_019_creek: <speak>That afternoon, we were swimming in the creek when the bushes moved.</speak>
narrator_020_shotgun: <speak>A man stepped out with a shotgun resting in the crook of his arm. A skinny kid about my age was right behind him.</speak>
dawes_001_stick_together: <speak>You're Earl's people? Good. Listen. Something big's been killing livestock around here. You stick together. And don't go wandering after dark.</speak>
narrator_021_hang_out: <speak>His son, Wyatt, asked if he could hang out with us.</speak>
narrator_022_eleven: <speak>By sunset, there were eleven of us.</speak>
narrator_024_around_seven: <speak>Around seven, Wyatt wanted to run home and ask his dad if he could sleep over.</speak>
narrator_025_dez_nia: <speak>My cousin Dez and a girl named Nia went with him. The rest of us stayed by the fire.</speak>
narrator_026_forty_minutes: <speak>About forty minutes later, the smell came back.</speak>
narrator_027_copper: <speak>Stronger this time. Like copper. Like the back of your throat after a nosebleed.</speak>
narrator_028_stoves: <speak>We checked the stoves in both trailers. Nothing was on.</speak>
narrator_030_burst_out: <speak>Wyatt, Dez and Nia burst out of the dark, sprinted straight past the fire, and threw themselves into the trailer.</speak>
wyatt_001_lock_door: <speak>Lock the door. Nobody goes outside. Nobody!</speak>
narrator_033_pig: <speak>A few days earlier, one of Wyatt's pigs had been torn open in his yard.</speak>
narrator_034_flashlight: <speak>Tonight, halfway back through the woods, Nia's flashlight had caught a man standing in the trees.</speak>
narrator_037_another: <speak>Then another, on the other side of the trail.</speak>
narrator_040_gibbering: <speak>Then a sound started up from both sides of the woods. A low, wet gibbering. Like someone trying to talk with a mouth that wasn't made for it.</speak>
narrator_041_jerking: <speak>Nia swung her light toward it and saw something jerking itself between the trees.</speak>
narrator_042_stepped_out: <speak>And when they finally saw our campfire, something stepped out onto the trail behind them.</speak>
narrator_043_ray_quiet: <speak>My little cousin Ray had gone very quiet.</speak>
narrator_046_stories: <speak>People around there told stories about something in those woods. A man's body. A goat's head.</speak>
narrator_047_never_see: <speak>Except you never see it like that.</speak>
narrator_049_walks_into: <speak>It walks into a group of people, sits down among them, and waits for somebody to notice there's one too many.</speak>
narrator_050_smell_stopped: <speak>And then, while Ray was still talking, the smell just stopped.</speak>
narrator_052_gone: <speak>It was there one second and gone the next.</speak>
narrator_053_local_guys: <speak>By morning, we'd decided it was some local guys messing with the city kid.</speak>
narrator_056_second_night: <speak>The second night, around one in the morning, we were telling ghost stories by the fire.</speak>
narrator_057_gagging: <speak>The smell came back so thick that one of the girls started gagging.</speak>
narrator_058_crowded: <speak>We crowded into the trailer and nobody wanted to go back out.</speak>
marcus_001_twelve: <speak>I didn't. There were twelve. One each for—</speak>
nia_001_get_it_out: <speak>Get it out! Get it out of here!</speak>
narrator_066_crashed: <speak>We crashed through the door and spilled out into the clearing.</speak>
narrator_069_sticks: <speak>We went back in with sticks and flashlights.</speak>
narrator_071_knee: <speak>Nia told us that just before she screamed, the person beside her had grabbed her knee and whispered into her ear.</speak>
narrator_075_sunrise: <speak>At sunrise, Nia and three others walked out of those woods and went home.</speak>
narrator_076_keys: <speak>I had my uncle's keys, so I had to stay. The others still thought it was a prank.</speak>
narrator_077_rifle: <speak>Wyatt went home to get his rifle.</speak>
narrator_078_seven_left: <speak>That left seven of us in the clearing.</speak>
narrator_079_at_least: <speak>At least, that's what we all said.</speak>
narrator_080_nia_back: <speak>At five-thirty, somebody said Nia was back.</speak>
narrator_081_fire_pit: <speak>She was standing by the dead fire pit.</speak>
narrator_084_silent: <speak>And the woods had gone completely silent. No birds. No insects. Nothing.</speak>
narrator_088_froze: <speak>One of the girls started walking out to her, then froze halfway.</speak>
narrator_089_blinds: <speak>We pulled every blind except one and watched her through it.</speak>
narrator_093_turned_to_watch: <speak>He said a girl by the fire had turned to watch him cross the clearing.</speak>
narrator_095_closer: <speak>But every time he looked back, she was closer.</speak>
narrator_096_went_pale: <speak>He stepped inside, looked around the room, and went pale.</speak>
wyatt_003_only_six: <speak>Marcus. Why are there only six of you?</speak>
narrator_097_math: <speak>Eleven of us. Four went home. Wyatt left.</speak>
narrator_100_math: <speak>None of us had done the math.</speak>
narrator_101_inside_again: <speak>It had been inside with us again.</speak>
narrator_102_when_it_left: <speak>And none of us had noticed when it left.</speak>
narrator_103_cole: <speak>At sundown, Wyatt's cousin Cole showed up with a lantern and a second rifle.</speak>
cole_001_little_friend: <speak>Where's your little friend at? She was standing in the middle of the trail. Kept lagging behind me. Just smiling.</speak>
narrator_104_reached: <speak>He'd reached out to touch her shoulder.</speak>
narrator_106_foot_left: <speak>She was standing a foot to the left.</speak>
narrator_109_scraped: <speak>Something scraped at the door. Half knocking. Half clawing.</speak>
narrator_113_no_rhythm: <speak>It had no rhythm at all. Like something that had listened to people for a very long time, but had never been one.</speak>
narrator_114_two_am: <speak>At two in the morning, Cole kicked the door open and fired into the sky.</speak>
narrator_117_scream: <speak>Then a scream, like a woman and an animal screaming at the same time.</speak>
narrator_118_crawled: <speak>Something low crawled out of the brush, straight toward the trailer.</speak>
narrator_119_fired: <speak>Cole fired, and it scrambled back into the dark.</speak>
narrator_121_never_door: <speak>But it never came back to the door.</speak>
narrator_123_wouldnt_look: <speak>Wyatt stayed behind to lock up. When he caught up with us, he was white as a sheet, and he wouldn't look at any of us.</speak>
narrator_124_two_days: <speak>Two days later, he told me why.</speak>
narrator_125_four_am: <speak>Around four that morning, he was fighting sleep in the chair by the door.</speak>
narrator_127_lay_down: <speak>Someone stepped out, picked its way between the sleeping bodies, and lay down right next to me.</speak>
narrator_132_didnt_scream: <speak>He didn't scream. In a trailer that small, in the dark, he could have shot any one of us.</speak>
narrator_133_pretending: <speak>So he sat there until morning, pretending to sleep, while every so often the thing beside me sat up, looked around at each of us<break time="420ms"/> and shook with that silent laugh.</speak>
narrator_134_window: <speak>When he went back to lock up, the bathroom window was wide open.</speak>
narrator_137_walked_out: <speak>And when we walked out of those woods, it walked out with us.</speak>
narrator_138_back_of_line: <speak>Right at the back of the line. All the way to Wyatt's house.</speak>
narrator_139_eyes: <speak>Then it stopped, looked Wyatt dead in the eyes<break time="420ms"/></speak>
narrator_142_chicago: <speak>I live in Chicago now. No woods. No trailers.</speak>
narrator_143_six_friends: <speak>Last weekend, I had six friends over to watch the game.</speak>
narrator_144_plates: <speak>I ordered pizza and set out the paper plates myself.</speak>
narrator_145_cleaning: <speak>When the game ended, I started cleaning up.</speak>
narrator_150_bathroom: <speak>And from down the hall, behind the bathroom door I always keep shut<break time="420ms"/></speak>
narrator_153_next_time: <speak>So the next time you eat with your friends<break time="420ms"/></speak>
